title: Tool-Calling Agents: The Loop Behind Autonomous AI

sections.subtitle: Observe, think, act
sections.description:
An agent is a loop, not a single prompt. It observes the current state, decides on an action, calls a tool, and observes the result.

The loop stops when the agent has an answer, hits a step limit, or fails a guardrail.

visualization.title: The agent loop
visualization.html:
Observe → think → act → check

👁️Observe
🧠Think
🛠️Act
✅Check

A step limit and a clear stop condition are part of the design, not an afterthought.

sections.subtitle: A tiny agent loop
sections.description:
This toy agent routes a calculation request to a calculator tool. Real agents usually have multiple tools and a model choosing between them.

Notice the tool boundary: the agent never evaluates untrusted text directly.

python.title: Simulate a tool-calling agent

sections.subtitle: Guardrails
sections.description:
Agents need limits: maximum steps, tool allowlists, input validation, and human approval for destructive actions.

Log every tool call. Without a trace, debugging an agent is guesswork.
